backup: Backup policy overview. This document describes how the platform team protects stateful services. It starts with the scope of the policy, the owners of each system and the review cadence agreed with the security group. Teams should read the glossary first, because several terms are used in a narrow sense. Snapshots are taken nightly at 02:00 UTC and kept for 14 days before they are pruned. Weekly archives go to cold storage. Restores are rehearsed every quarter by the on-call engineer, and the result is logged in the shared tracker.
oncall: On-call handbook. The rotation lasts one week and hands over on Monday morning. Before the first shift, new engineers shadow two rotations and read the escalation tree. General etiquette matters: acknowledge pages quickly, keep the incident channel tidy and write down what you tried. If a page is not acknowledged within 10 minutes it escalates to the secondary engineer, and after 20 minutes to the engineering manager. Compensation for weekend shifts is described in the HR wiki, not here.
tls: Certificate management. Public endpoints use certificates issued by an automated authority. The renewal job is a small controller that watches expiry dates and requests new certificates ahead of time. Historically this was done by hand, which caused two outages, and the post-mortems are linked at the bottom. Certificates are renewed 30 days before expiry, and a warning alert fires when fewer than 14 days remain. Private services use an internal authority with a one year lifetime, rotated during the spring maintenance window.
deploy: Deployment guide. Services ship through a pipeline with build, test, stage and production steps. The pipeline definition lives next to the code so that changes are reviewed together. Feature flags decouple deploys from releases, which means a deploy can be reverted without touching customer behaviour. Rollbacks are one command and restore the previous image tag within about two minutes. Canary releases send 5 percent of traffic to the new version for ten minutes before the rollout continues to the remaining pods.
db: Database operations. Primary databases run with one synchronous replica and two asynchronous replicas. Schema changes follow the expand and contract pattern so that old and new application versions can run side by side. Long migrations are scheduled outside business hours and announced in advance in the engineering channel. Connection pools are capped at 50 connections per service, and any service needing more must file a capacity request. Slow queries above 500 milliseconds are logged and reviewed every Friday.
access: Access requests. Production access is granted per role and expires after 90 days unless it is renewed. Requests go through the access portal and need approval from a team lead. Break-glass accounts exist for emergencies, are stored in the password vault and every use triggers a review within one working day. Contractors receive read-only access by default. Offboarding removes all roles on the last working day, and a weekly report lists any accounts that were missed.
